body:
**Roadmap:** [`docs/roadmap/leanisa-blueprint.md`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/leanerVM/blob/main/docs/roadmap/leanisa-blueprint.md) — the specification of what is wanted; changed only by pull request; never records status.
**Status:** [`docs/roadmap/leanisa-status.md`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/leanerVM/blob/main/docs/roadmap/leanisa-status.md) — where it stands; rewritten whole when a layer lands.
**Target:** [leanEthereum/leanVM](https://github.com/leanEthereum/leanVM) at [`a386121f`](https://github.com/leanEthereum/leanVM/commit/a386121f84292f6fa663aaa3e570c15bc0240ea2). Specification source: [`doc/leanvm/`](https://github.com/leanEthereum/leanVM/tree/a386121f84292f6fa663aaa3e570c15bc0240ea2/doc/leanvm) at the pin; leanVM's CI renders it as [leanVM.pdf](https://github.com/leanEthereum/leanVM/releases/download/doc-latest/leanVM.pdf) (linked from the leanVM README), rebuilt on every push to leanVM's `main`, so it tracks `main`, not the pin. Implementation: [`crates/lean_vm/src/`](https://github.com/leanEthereum/leanVM/tree/a386121f84292f6fa663aaa3e570c15bc0240ea2/crates/lean_vm/src).

Both documents link back here (roadmap section *How work is tracked*). This issue holds nothing that is not in them; where they disagree, the files win.

Related: #3 (Flock, owns the BLAKE2s circuit, consumes `CompressCells` and owes `Blake2sRelation`, the `BLAKE2S` table's `Assumptions` since Layer 6 and `SatisfiedBy`'s conjunct `Blake2sRowsValid` since Layer 8); #12 (the proof-system roadmap, which proves `SatisfiedBy`; its requests #13 are settled in the roadmap); #16 and #20 (the Clean balance request Layer 9 waits on); #23 (Layer 8's three named hypotheses fold into Clean #446's fixed columns and proof-committed data, decision 15). Upstream: Clean [#446](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/pull/446), [#452](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/clean/issues/452); CompPoly [#322](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/CompPoly/issues/322).

## What this roadmap builds

One executable semantics `step : Program → MemImage κ → Regs → Option Regs` for leanISA over CompPoly's `K = GF(2^64)`, `E = GF(2^192)`; the six M3 tables, the memory/bytecode seed–finalize blocks, and the verifier boundary as Clean components over six pull/push channels; `Constraints.SatisfiedBy` and `Constraints.AssignmentRepresents` on Clean's `EnsembleWitness`; and the theorems `constraintSoundness` and `constraintCompleteness`, both for well-formed bytecode (`WellFormedBytecode prog`). Pins: leanVM `a386121f`, CompPoly `3468b38c`, Clean `93c9d1ef`, Lean `v4.33.1`. Priorities: auditability of the trusted surface, fidelity to the pinned sources, landed proofs only (no `sorry`; a target whose dependency is not yet available is a block comment at its place).

## Layer checklist

Tick a layer only when its pull request has merged with `./scripts/validate.sh` green and the layer's acceptance tests in `tests/`. Link the PR on the line.

- [x] **Dependencies** — Clean `93c9d1ef` wired in beside CompPoly; builds under `v4.33.1`; `FiniteField BF64` verified. (#5)
- [x] **Layer 0 — fields, limbs, generator.** `K`, `E`, `ofK`, limbs, `IsInK`, `IsCanonical128`, `instance FiniteField K`; `g = 0x2` with the seven `decide +kernel` order checks and `orderOf_g`; `gpow`, `gpow_injOn`. Enables the kernel axiom audit. (#6)
- [x] **Layer 1 — BLAKE2s.** RFC `iv`/`sigma`; tree-mode `compress` (two flag words); `cellWords`, `unpackMetadata`, `CompressCells`; RFC vectors plus the Rust word-order vector with its dump command. (#7)
- [x] **Layer 2 — instructions, image, public input.** `Opcode`, caps, `DerefMode`, `Instr`, `Instr.opcode`, `Program`, `gLog?` (noncomputable) with `gLog?_spec`, `MemImage.read`, `PublicInput`. (#8)
- [x] **Layer 3 — `step`, `ValidExecution`.** Written from specification §2 first, diffed against `cpu/execute.rs` after; fixtures are kernel-checked proofs through the fetch and read lemmas on the Rust `mul_192bit_word` program, the `BLAKE2S` executor row, a taken `JUMP`, a `DEREF` in `pc` mode, and the rejections of acceptance tests 2–7 and 12. `execute_of_step`, the join between a program's step and an instruction's execution, added with #21. (#11)
- [x] **Layer 4 — bytecode encoding.** `derefFlags`, `entry`, `encodeSlots`, `decode`, `decode_entry`, `decode_eq_some_iff`, `entry_injective`. (#9)
- [x] **Layer 5 — channels.** `Regs` (now field-parametric, the state message)/`MemMsg`/`BytecodeMsg`; `st/mem/bc × pull/push` with `Guarantees` against the image for the memory pull, static decodability for the bytecode pull (program- and data-free since decision 14, #21), none for the state pull; `memRows`, `imageOf`, `WellShapedData` (the `"bytecode"` table and `programOf` left with #21); `channelSep`, `channelDir`, `busTuple`, the three `toElements` lemmas; `memRead`, `bytecodeRead` through `Channel.pull`/`Channel.push`. `BytecodePull.Guarantees` strengthened by Layer 6 to name the fetched instruction on both sides (F7) and reduced to its decoding half by decision 14 (#21). (#17)
- [x] **Layer 6 — six opcode tables.** `xorTable`, `mulTable`, `setTable`, `derefTable`, `jumpTable`, `blake2sTable`: one `GeneralFormalCircuit K Row Regs` each, returning the state it pushes (decision 10), with soundness and completeness; per table the relation `*Bindings mem r`, `*Refines mem r next` (over `execute` of the row's own instruction, program-free since decision 14, #21), `*_refines_iff`, the adapter `*Spec` as `Spec`, and the honest row `*RowOf`, `*RowOf_refines`, `*_exec_complete` (decision 11, F8); `storeCoords_eval`, `flags_sound`/`flags_complete`, `jumpEnv`/`jump_env_iff`, `Blake2sRelation` (the one named assumption), `blake2sRow_complete`; `mul_limbs`, `E.ofCell` (Layer 0), `MemImage.limbsAt`/`cellAt` (Layer 2), `decode_deref_eq_some_iff` (Layer 4). Reviewed 2026-09-14, `docs/reviews/leanisa-layer6-tables.md`. Tests: a satisfying row from every valid execution of the fixture (three `DEREF` modes, both `JUMP` branches), mutated rows rejected through each table's `soundness`, the `BLAKE2S` boundary row. (#19)
- [x] **Layer 7 — boundary blocks.** `PublicIO` (the four lanes), `MemRow`/`memTable`, `BytecodeRow`/`bytecodeTable`, `leanIsaVerifier prog`: each block its two flushes with no constraint, its `Spec` its pull guarantee (`MemSpec`; `BytecodeDecodes`, program-free), the verifier's `True` and a function of the public program, pulling `Expression.const prog.finalPc` (decisions 12 and 14, F9); the honest rows `memRowOf`/`bytecodeRowOf` with `mem_word_complete`/`bytecode_entry_complete`; `BytecodeBindings prog` as the per-row reading of Layer 8's conjunct; `verifier_push_eval`/`verifier_pull_eval`. With it, decision 14 (the program left the prover data: `programOf` gone, the channels and the six tables program-free; closes #22), the faithfulness review of `main` against leanVM (`docs/reviews/leanvm-faithfulness-review.md`) and the citation refresh of its row 20. (#21)
- [x] **Layer 8 — statement.** `leanIsaEnsemble prog` (eight components, six channels, `leanIsaVerifier prog`; program-bearing through the verifier alone), the readers of a witness (`tableAt`, `blake2sRows`, `memBlockRows`, `bytecodeBlockRows`, `messagesOn`/`rowMessagesOn` by channel name, `memRowAt`, `blake2sRowAt`), `BalancedPair` (a `List.Perm` of the messages on a channel pair, counted in ℕ, never Clean's field sum), `CountsNonzero` (the six tables' read counts, as leanVM's count channel stacks them), `Caps` (the M3 part of `read_public`: the `log_mem` window, power-of-two heights over all eight tables, the `BLAKE2S` floor), the three named hypotheses over the blocks' raw rows (`IndexColumnsAreRowIndices`, `SeedRowsAreTheImage`, `BytecodeRowsAreTheProgram prog`; decision 15, #23), `Blake2sRowsValid` (the BLAKE2s validity Flock proves, the one conjunct outside the bus; review finding A1) with `assumptions_of_blake2sRowsValid` turning it into Clean's `w.Assumptions`, `SatisfiedBy prog input w` (a structure of thirteen named conjuncts, the public words through `MemImage.read`), `RowSteps`/`AssignmentRepresents` (a structure; `assignmentRepresents_image`); `rowAt_toElements`, `memRowAt_toElements`, `blake2sRowAt_toElements`, `mem_tables_iff`, `tableAt_component`. Layer 9's four statements are block comments at the end of `Statement.lean`. Reviewed 2026-09-17, `docs/reviews/leanisa-layer8-statement.md` (A1, A2 load-bearing; all met). Tests: one hand-built witness for the executor's `mul_192bit_word` with fill blocks (`κ = 16`, the `2^16`-row block never enumerated, E8): `fill_satisfiedBy`, `fill_represents`, `fill_t1_instance`; seven rejections, each failing the conjunct named (a wrong finalize count, a balancing zero count `zero_count_witness`, a wrong digest, a shifted index column, a wrong public word, two bad heights). (#24)
- [ ] **Layer 9 — bus soundness.** `mem_channel_sound`, `bytecode_channel_sound` (the strong form: every pulled entry is the program's at its counter), `no_row_at_sentinel`, `exists_run_of_balanced`. Consumes Clean's direction-tagged, ℕ-counted balance (contract in the roadmap's dependency table; #16, #20); the four statements are in place as block comments at the end of `Statement.lean` since Layer 8 (#24) and take their proofs when Clean's balance lands.
- [ ] **Layer 10 — T1.** `HasFillBlocks`, `WellFormedBytecode`; `constraintSoundness` and `constraintCompleteness` under `WellFormedBytecode prog`.

Ordering: Layers 0, 1, 4 independent; 2 needs 0; 3 needs 1–2; 5 needs 3–4; 6 and 7 need 5; 8 needs 6–7; 9 needs 8 and the Clean change; 10 needs 9.

## Frontier

- **Layer 8 landed** as #24 (`feat/leanisa-statement`, merged 2026-09-18 as `8563b05`) and is ticked above; the status file was rewritten whole in the same change. The statement is `SatisfiedBy prog input w`, a structure of named conjuncts that Layers 9 and 10 project by name: the public IO is the run's lanes; Clean's `w.Constraints` (the `JUMP` residuals, since no other component has an assertion); the three channel pairs balance as `List.Perm`s of the messages on the named channels, never Clean's field sum (`ringChar K = 2` makes that sum accept at most one interaction, C10); the six tables' read counts are nonzero; the caps; the three named hypotheses; every `BLAKE2S` row satisfies `Blake2sRelation`; and the two public words. Review finding A1 (high) is the one that changed the statement: Clean's `EnsembleWitness.Constraints` excludes a table's `Assumptions` and its `AssumptionsConsistency` sources them from the public input alone, so without `Blake2sRowsValid` the statement accepted a wrong-but-canonical digest and `constraintSoundness` was false for any program executing `BLAKE2S`; `assumptions_of_blake2sRowsValid` hands the conjunct to Clean's `TableSoundness`, which Layer 10 applies directly. The Flock design note's D5 later replaces the conjunct by the constraints themselves. A2 (medium): the count-`0` rejection also failed balance, so `zero_count_witness` balances a zero-count read and fails `CountsNonzero` alone. Seven sketch adjustments are written into the roadmap (structures with named fields; channels by name, since `RawChannel` has no decidable equality; `CountsNonzero` over `w.tables.take 6`; `Caps.heights` over all eight tables; the hypotheses through `memRowAt` and `List.ofFn`; the public words through `MemImage.read`; `RowSteps` as occurrence, not an injection). Decision 15 (#23) records what Clean #446 removes.
- **Decision 14 (settled 2026-09-16; #21, closes #22):** the program is public, and the channels and the tables are program-free. The faithfulness review of `main` against leanVM `a386121f` (`docs/reviews/leanvm-faithfulness-review.md`; a 21-row divergence table, every first-party Lean file read against the specification and the Rust, all six tables matching) found Layers 5 to 7 reading the program off Clean's `ProverData` (`programOf`), a field of the witness, where leanVM's bytecode is public and never committed (§6.4; `layout.rs:288-290`, `Coord::Public`): finding F10. Decision 13's fix, `prog : Program` as a parameter of the channels, the six tables and the bytecode block, was built and discarded the same day: it made every AIR a function of the program, where leanVM's are fixed for all programs (a table's bytecode flush is its constant opcode and its own operand columns, `tables.rs:143-152`), and it bought no soundness, the bytecode block still needing the statement's conjunct to pin its seed rows. Instead: `BytecodePull.Guarantees` is static decodability, naming no program and reading no data; each table's relation is `*Refines mem r next` over `execute` of the instruction the row's own columns name, joined to a program's step by Layer 3's `execute_of_step`; the bytecode block's `Spec` is `BytecodeDecodes r`; and the program enters in three places, `bytecodeRowOf prog`, `leanIsaVerifier prog` and Layer 8's `SatisfiedBy prog`, whose conjunct `BytecodeRowsAreTheProgram prog` says the block's rows are the program's with only the finalize counts free, as the verifier forms them itself (§8.5, Bus 4), and which Clean #446's fixed columns make a primitive. The declared cost: a table no longer rejects a row naming an instruction the program does not hold at its counter; that is the bus's (Layer 9), as it is for leanVM's AIR. `programOf`, the `"bytecode"` table, `BytecodeSpec` and the conjunct `programOf w.data = prog` are gone (pinned convention "Program", acceptance test 22; status decision 14, findings F7, F10). Also from the review: R27 (the verifier accepts any `K`-array as bytecode; T1 is stated for decodable bytecode), the R3 addendum, and the line-citation refresh (its row 20, done in #21).
- **Layer 7 landed** as #21 (`feat/leanisa-boundary`): decision 12, a boundary block's `Spec` is its pull guarantee and the verifier's is `True`; revised on review so that the verifier is a function of the program, `leanIsaVerifier prog` pulling `Expression.const prog.finalPc` as `layout.rs:357` writes `Const(g_pow(final_pc))` into the block, with `PublicIO` the four lanes (finding F9).
- Layers 0 (#6), 1 (#7), 2 (#8), 3 (#11), 4 (#9), 5 (#17), 6 (#19), 7 (#21) and 8 (#24) are merged; Layers 0 to 4 were reviewed together on 2026-09-10, Layer 6 on 2026-09-14 (`docs/reviews/leanisa-layer6-tables.md`) and Layer 8 on 2026-09-17 (`docs/reviews/leanisa-layer8-statement.md`; status file, frontier). Nothing in this roadmap can start now without an upstream change: Layer 9's proofs consume Clean's direction-tagged, ℕ-counted balance (#16, #20) and Layer 10 consumes Layer 9; Layer 8's refactor #23 waits on Clean #446 and a pin bump that survives P3. The statement surface of T1 is complete: `fill_t1_instance` is the completeness instance for the fixture program, by hand.
- **Decision 10 (#19):** the six tables return the state they push (`GeneralFormalCircuit K Row Regs`, not `… unit`), so every `Spec` names the successor, the `JUMP` successor being a function of its witness `b`.
- **Decision 11 (#19; review R1, R2; F8):** a table's `Spec` is its functional specification `*Spec r next data := *Refines (imageOf data).2 r next`, where `*Refines mem r next` is a structure over an explicit image (`bindings : *Bindings mem r`, the row's input words bound to the image as named facts; `exec_eq`, the execution of the instruction the row's own columns name; first built over a program and an image with `step_eq`, made program-free by decision 14), with `*_refines_iff` as the opcode-level reading; `ProverAssumptions` is the honest prover's row `∃ next, *Spec r next data`, proved of the row of any valid execution (`*RowOf_refines`), so nothing above the tables assumes it. `BLAKE2S` keeps `Blake2sRelation r` as `Assumptions` and `Blake2sBindings` as its prover premise: the table proves the binding, Flock (#3) owes the compression, `blake2sRow_complete` states the boundary. A table file states the circuit, its `Spec` and the honest row, and nothing else; Layer 4 facts live in Layer 4.
- **F7 (#19):** the roadmap's bytecode guarantee `fetch pc = decode entry` was satisfied by an undecodable entry at a non-address, under which `derefTable`'s soundness was false; Layer 6 made `BytecodePull.Guarantees` name the fetched instruction on both sides, and decision 14 (#21) keeps the decoding half alone, `∃ ins, decode entry = some ins`, which is what `DEREF` uses; the fetch half is Layer 9's `bytecode_channel_sound`, which Theorem 6.4 gives from balance and the block's rows.
- **E6, E7 (#19, status file):** core's `BitVec` simprocs fire on `K` numerals, so proofs over `K` use `simp only` and exclude `BitVec.reduceNeg`; `circuit_norm` rewrites under a witness program's `decide` while leaving its instance on the old terms, so `jump_env_iff` rewrites the conditional first. Clean's `Circuit.witgen` carries no data; an executable, data-aware row generator is T2's.
- **E8 (#24, status file; the roadmap's "Large witnesses" convention):** a definitional comparison of a stuck projection against a `List.ofFn`, or of the data's log-size against a numeral, makes both the elaborator and the kernel evaluate the `2^16`-row memory block (`maxRecDepth`, "(kernel) deep recursion detected"); the tests prove `imageOf fillData = ⟨minLogMem, fillImage⟩` once and substitute over a destructured witness, read the block through `getElem?`, and decide interactions through `Component.rowOperations` after `table_interactions_eq`, since the kernel does not unfold `Component.operations`.
- **F6 (decision 9):** the constraints let a `JUMP` in the sentinel slot execute, so `constraintSoundness` as first stated was false. Both T1 theorems now take `WellFormedBytecode prog` (`sentinelHalts`, `hasFillBlocks`); Layer 9 gains `no_row_at_sentinel`; Layer 3 is unchanged (roadmap acceptance test 20).
- **Decision 7 (#10):** the state pull carries no guarantee; Layer 9 states Proposition 6.1 as `exists_run_of_balanced` (acceptance test 21).
- **Decision 8 (#13):** `Caps` requires power-of-two heights and the bytecode length; each channel names its separator, direction and sixteen-slot tuple.
- **Decision 6:** the roadmap's Layer 1 types the flags as `UInt32` words, as the landed code does.
- Three findings from Layer 0 bind later layers (status file, findings C8, P1, P3): Clean is not a `module`, so it is consumed from plain files and Layers 5–10 are plain files; CompPoly's `Ext` arithmetic does not reduce in the kernel from a `module` file, so kernel-decided fixtures live in plain test files; an executable linking CompPoly's `BF64` module is killed at startup, so `lake test` builds the test library and no leanerVM executable may link the field module.
- `gLog?` is `noncomputable` (Layer 2, #8), so `step` and `ValidExecution` are specifications that cannot be run: a fixture is a proof unfolding `run` through `Program.fetch_gpow` and `MemImage.read_gpow`, not a `decide`.
- Both Rust vectors are dumped mechanically (`scripts/dump-blake2s-rust.sh`, `scripts/dump-mul-rust.sh`).
- The Clean bus change (direction tag + multiset balance) is the only external item on the critical path; #16 tracks the combined request, whose action is a pull request to Clean (#452 covers half), with the kernel-checked exhibits of finding C10 from the Layer 5 tests. Clean #446 removes the three Layer 8 hypotheses (#23, decision 15): `IndexColumnsAreRowIndices` becomes a fixed column `fun i ↦ g^i` on `memTable`, `BytecodeRowsAreTheProgram prog` fixed entry columns on `bytecodeTable prog`, and `SeedRowsAreTheImage` the `"mem"` table derived from the block's committed columns; nothing else in `SatisfiedBy` moves, and Layer 9's channel theorems then take their seed facts from the components.

## Decisions pending

Numbers are the status file's. Settled: 1 (`DEREF` reads `fp·o3` in every mode), 2 (T1 for well-formed programs), 4 (fixtures are kernel proofs in plain test files; Layer 6's row tests the same, against `E.ofLimbs` words), 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 (a boundary block's `Spec` is its pull guarantee, the verifier's `True`, and the verifier is a function of the program), 13 (superseded by 14), 14 (the program is public and the channels and tables are program-free; it enters through `bytecodeRowOf prog`, `leanIsaVerifier prog` and `SatisfiedBy prog`; #21).

3. Bytecode stays on the bus, not a Clean `StaticTable` lookup.
5. Restoring a test executable (finding P3): needs CompPoly to drop `[Fintype F]` from `Ext`'s runtime signature and make `Fintype BF64` noncomputable, a pin bump; until then tests are compile-time `#guard`s and `example`s.
15. Clean #446 (#23): Layer 8's three named hypotheses become fixed columns and proof-committed data when the PR merges and the Clean pin is bumped (the bump also has to survive P3, item 5); until then they are conjuncts of `SatisfiedBy` over the blocks' raw rows, and the Layer 8 tests reject their violations by name.

## How to work on this

- **Claim a slice:** open an issue titled `[Intention]: leanISA Layer N: …` listing the exact declaration names taken, link it here, close it with the PR.
- **Report a problem with the roadmap:** open `[Roadmap]: leanISA: …` naming the layer and the acceptance test or convention it touches.
- **Change the roadmap:** open a pull request that edits `docs/roadmap/leanisa-blueprint.md`, titled `docs(leanisa): …`, and reference #4 in its description so it is listed in this issue's timeline; say which layer, acceptance test, or convention it touches. A pull request that lands a layer rewrites `docs/roadmap/leanisa-status.md` whole (header commit, coverage table, frontier) in the same change and ticks the layer above with the PR link. A decision taken on a pending item is written into the roadmap, as the convention or acceptance test it settles, and removed from the status file and from this issue.
- **Per PR:** statement reviewed independently of proof; every hypothesis in the signature; inhabitant and negative control under `tests/`; Category A written from the specification first; Category B cites section, file, lines, pin; helpers `private`; no `sorry`/`admit`/`axiom`/`unsafe`/`native_decide`; label `awaiting-review` when done, `awaiting-author` after a review.
title: roadmap: scaffold leanISA semantics and M3 constraints on CompPoly and Clean
